title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Implementation Measures for the Pilot Work of People's Courts in Adjudicating Public Interest Litigation Cases Initiated by People's Procuratorates
keywords_en: administrative litigation; public interest litigation initiated by the people's procuratorate
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Implementation Measures for the Pilot Work of People's Courts Trying Public Interest Litigation Cases Initiated by People's Procuratorates

Fa Fa [2016] No. 6

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

In order to fully implement the spirit of the Fourth Plenary Session of the Eighteenth Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, fulfill the judicial reform task of exploring public interest litigation initiated by procuratorial organs as deployed by the Central Committee, and ensure the correct adjudication of public interest litigation cases initiated by People's Procuratorates, in accordance with the "Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Authorizing the Supreme People's Procuratorate to Carry Out Pilot Work on Public Interest Litigation in Certain Areas," this Court has formulated the "Implementation Measures for the Pilot Work of People's Courts Trying Public Interest Litigation Cases Initiated by People's Procuratorates." These Implementation Measures were adopted at the 1679th session of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on February 22, 2016, and are hereby issued, effective as of March 1, 2016. People's Courts in all pilot areas shall earnestly implement them. For important circumstances and issues encountered during implementation, please promptly report to the Supreme People's Court.

February 25, 2016

Implementation Measures for the Pilot Work of People's Courts Trying Public Interest Litigation Cases Initiated by People's Procuratorates

For the purpose of implementing the "Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Authorizing the Supreme People's Procuratorate to Carry Out Pilot Work on Public Interest Litigation in Certain Areas," and to lawfully adjudicate public interest litigation cases initiated by People's Procuratorates, these Measures are formulated in accordance with the provisions of the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," the "Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," and other laws, and in light of the actual circumstances of trial work.

I. Civil Public Interest Litigation

Article 1 Where a People's Procuratorate believes that a defendant has engaged in conduct that harms the public interest, such as polluting the environment, destroying the ecology, or infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of numerous consumers in the field of food and drug safety, and where there is no qualified entity to initiate a lawsuit or a qualified entity does not initiate a lawsuit, and the People's Procuratorate initiates a civil public interest lawsuit with a People's Court that meets the requirements of subparagraphs (2), (3), and (4) of Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court shall register the case.

Article 2 A People's Procuratorate initiating a civil public interest lawsuit shall submit the following materials:

(1) A complaint that complies with Article 121 of the Civil Procedure Law, together with copies according to the number of defendants;
(2) Preliminary evidentiary materials showing conduct that harms the public interest, such as polluting the environment, destroying the ecology, or infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of numerous consumers in the field of food and drug safety;
(3) Evidentiary materials showing that the People's Procuratorate has fulfilled the pre-litigation procedures of urging or supporting the organs or relevant organizations prescribed by law to initiate a civil public interest lawsuit.

Article 3 A People's Procuratorate initiating a civil public interest lawsuit may make claims requesting the defendant to cease the infringement, remove the obstruction, eliminate the danger, restore the original condition, compensate for losses, or make an apology, among other claims.

Article 4 When a People's Procuratorate initiates a civil public interest lawsuit in its capacity as a public interest litigator, its litigation rights and obligations shall be determined by reference to the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law concerning the litigation rights and obligations of the plaintiff. The defendant in a civil public interest lawsuit is the citizen, legal person, or other organization that is alleged to have committed the conduct harming the public interest.

Article 5 First-instance civil public interest litigation cases initiated by a People's Procuratorate shall be under the jurisdiction of the Intermediate People's Court of the place where the infringing act occurred, where the harmful result occurred, or where the defendant is domiciled, unless otherwise provided by law or judicial interpretation.

Article 6 In adjudicating a civil public interest litigation case initiated by a People's Procuratorate, if the defendant raises a counterclaim, the People's Court shall not accept it.

Article 7 In adjudicating a first-instance civil public interest litigation case initiated by a People's Procuratorate, the People's Court shall, in principle, apply the people's assessor system. If a party applies for the case not to be tried under the people's assessor system, the People's Court may, upon review, decide not to apply the people's assessor system.

Article 8 After the People's Procuratorate and the defendant reach a settlement agreement or a mediation agreement, the People's Court shall publish the content of the agreement, with the publication period being no less than thirty days. After the expiration of the publication period, if the People's Court concludes upon review that the content of the settlement agreement or the mediation agreement does not harm the public interest, it shall issue a consent judgment.

Article 9 If the People's Procuratorate applies for withdrawal of the lawsuit before the closing of the court debate, or after the closing of the court debate when all of the claims of the People's Procuratorate have been fulfilled and it applies for withdrawal, such withdrawal shall be permitted.

Article 10 With respect to the judgment or ruling of the People's Court in a civil public interest litigation case, if a party files an appeal according to law, a People's Procuratorate initiates a protest according to law, or another party files an application for retrial according to law that meets the requirements of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law, the case shall be tried respectively in accordance with the second-instance procedure or the trial supervision procedure provided for in the Civil Procedure Law.

II. Administrative Public Interest Litigation

Article 11 Where a People's Procuratorate believes that an administrative organ with regulatory and supervisory duties in fields such as ecological environment and resource protection, state asset protection, or state-owned land use rights concession, or an organization authorized by laws, regulations, or rules, has illegally exercised its functions and powers or failed to perform its statutory duties, thereby causing harm to the state and social public interests, and the People's Procuratorate initiates an administrative public interest lawsuit with a People's Court that meets the requirements of subparagraphs (2), (3), and (4) of Article 49 of the Administrative Procedure Law, the People's Court shall register the case.

Article 12 A People's Procuratorate initiating an administrative public interest lawsuit shall submit the following materials:

(1) A complaint for administrative public interest litigation, together with copies according to the number of defendants;
(2) Preliminary evidentiary materials showing that the conduct of the defendant has caused harm to the state and social public interests;
(3) Evidentiary materials showing that the People's Procuratorate has fulfilled the pre-litigation procedure of issuing a procuratorial recommendation to the relevant administrative organ, urging it to correct the illegal administrative act or perform its duties according to law.

Article 13 A People's Procuratorate initiating an administrative public interest lawsuit may make claims to the People's Court seeking revocation or partial revocation of the illegal administrative act, performance of statutory duties within a certain period, or confirmation that the administrative act is unlawful or invalid, among other claims.

Article 14 When a People's Procuratorate initiates an administrative public interest lawsuit in its capacity as a public interest litigator, its litigation rights and obligations shall be determined by reference to the provisions of the Administrative Procedure Law concerning the litigation rights and obligations of the plaintiff. The defendant in an administrative public interest lawsuit is the administrative organ exercising functions and powers or bearing administrative duties in fields such as ecological environment and resource protection, state asset protection, or state-owned land use rights concession, as well as organizations authorized by laws, regulations, or rules.

Article 15 First-instance administrative public interest litigation cases initiated by a People's Procuratorate shall be under the jurisdiction of the Basic People's Court of the place where the administrative organ that initially made the administrative act is located. For cases that have been reconsidered, they may also be under the jurisdiction of the Basic People's Court of the place where the reconsideration organ is located. Cases where a People's Procuratorate initiates a public interest lawsuit against an administrative act made by a department of the State Council or a local people's government at or above the county level, as well as major and complex public interest litigation cases within the jurisdiction, shall be under the jurisdiction of the Intermediate People's Court.

Article 16 In adjudicating a first-instance administrative public interest litigation case initiated by a People's Procuratorate, the People's Court shall, in principle, apply the people's assessor system.

Article 17 In adjudicating an administrative public interest litigation case initiated by a People's Procuratorate, the People's Court shall not apply mediation.

Article 18 Before the People's Court pronounces the judgment or ruling in an administrative public interest litigation case, if the People's Procuratorate applies for withdrawal of the lawsuit, whether to permit such withdrawal shall be determined by the People's Court by ruling.

Article 19 With respect to the judgment or ruling of the People's Court in an administrative public interest litigation case, if a party files an appeal according to law, a People's Procuratorate initiates a protest according to law, or another party files an application for retrial that meets the requirements of Article 91 of the Administrative Procedure Law, the case shall be tried respectively in accordance with the second-instance procedure or the trial supervision procedure provided for in the Administrative Procedure Law.

III. Other Provisions

Article 20 People's Courts adjudicating public interest litigation cases initiated by a People's Procuratorate shall conduct the trial openly in accordance with law. People's Courts may invite deputies to the People's Congress and members of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) to observe the trial, and may satisfy the need of the public and media to understand the actual situation of the trial through means such as live broadcast or recorded broadcast of the trial. Judicial documents shall be publicly released on the internet in accordance with the relevant provisions.

Article 21 If a People's Court, when adjudicating a public interest litigation case initiated by a People's Procuratorate, deems that a judicial recommendation should be made, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the "Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Strengthening the Work of Judicial Recommendations."

Article 22 In a public interest litigation case initiated by a People's Procuratorate, the People's Procuratorate shall be exempt from paying the litigation fees as specified in Article 6 of the "Measures for the Payment of Litigation Fees."

Article 23 For matters not provided for in these Measures in the adjudication of public interest litigation cases initiated by a People's Procuratorate, the provisions of the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," the "Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," and relevant judicial interpretations shall apply.

IV. Supplementary Provisions

Article 24 These Measures shall apply to the following thirteen provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government: Beijing, Inner Mongolia, Jilin, Jiangsu, Anhui, Fujian, Shandong, Hubei, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Shaanxi, and Gansu.

Article 25 These Measures shall come into effect as of March 1, 2016.
